canonical_definition:
What it is. Papers most commonly describe this instrument as an external safety evaluator: a harmfulness detection model that assigns a probability score indicating whether a given response is harmful. In Refusal-Aware Red Teaming: Exposing Inconsistency in Safety Evaluations, it is used among "state-of-the-art harmfulness detection models" that assign harmfulness probabilities to each response.

What it is claimed to measure. The available description uses it to score whether a response is harmful by assigning a harmfulness probability. No constructs and no behavioral indicators are linked to it through recorded measurement claims.

Space of uses. The only described usage places it alongside WildGuard as part of an evaluation setup, where both models act as external safety evaluators for response harmfulness. No other measurement instrument is linked to it.
